title: 35-second versus 45-second scheduled scan window: isolated virtual-clock evidence

platformCondition.verification: Parent independently re-read cloud_fn_info; saved local read-only tool response also confirms these exact whitelisted fields.
platformCondition.constraint: 45 seconds is assessed only against the currently verified 60-second function timeout. Re-evaluate if that timeout changes.

method.initialInventory: unavailable, no alert events, empty notification queue except slow_notification scenarios
method.accountFollowIndexes: Present and valid; no legacy per-account follow lookup fallback.
method.clock: A deterministic asynchronous timer queue advances to the next scheduled completion; overlapping operations consume concurrent, not additive, elapsed time.
method.database: Each repository method awaits the configured synthetic delay, then runs the existing in-memory repository implementation. Atomic transaction logic, lease ownership, quota decisions and application code remain active.
method.http: AbortSignal.timeout budgets are recorded; the simulated fetch completes at min(response delay, granted timeout). Exceeding that timeout throws a TimeoutError, so deadline-truncated requests do not count as successful coverage.
method.notification: slow_notification scenarios seed one valid pending task for a confirmed available target, use an 8-second simulated message call bounded by the options.timeoutMs supplied by notifier, and retain actual claim/reservation/settlement code.
method.workBudget: Explicit runScheduled maxRunMs is 35000 or 45000. Source files were not edited by this experiment.
method.measuredEndpoint: Await runScheduled resolution, including scheduler drain, settleNotifications and collector lease release.
method.successfulUniqueGroupsDefinition: Distinct storeNumber values whose simulated HTTP response completed successfully before its assigned timeout. The generated response is a valid known-stock observation.
method.scannedDefinition: The production result.scanned count includes persisted unknown observations and may include repeated phase visits; it is not unique successful coverage.
method.lateDatabaseStall: All repository methods starting at or after maxRunMs - 1000 switch to an 8000ms delay; this is an adversarial boundary test, not a production measurement.

keyFindings: With 200ms repository methods and 800ms HTTP, 35 -> 45 seconds improves successful unique coverage from 30/31 to 31/31; elapsed time including cleanup is 35.4 -> 45.8 seconds.
With 300ms repository methods and 800ms HTTP, successful coverage is 22/31 -> 30/31 after honoring shortened HTTP budgets; 45 seconds still does not guarantee every group.
At 45 seconds, tested ordinary and slow DB/HTTP/message cases finish between 25.8 and 54 seconds, excluding entry/cold-start overhead.
At 45 seconds with 200ms repository latency there are 39 attempts but only 31 unique successful groups; 8 attempts revisit groups in a subsequent phase.
An adversarial late 8-second DB stall exceeds the 60-second platform timeout under both 35- and 45-second work windows (66 and 68 seconds), and loses the collector lease.
No test result establishes absence of missed notifications or real WeChat receipt.
limitations: Synthetic repository-method latency is not a per-CloudBase-RPC latency; production transactions can contain multiple reads/writes and retries.
No platform hard kill was applied at 60 seconds, so adversarial results above 60 seconds are diagnostic counterexamples rather than deployable completion guarantees.
Timing starts at runScheduled entry and excludes module cold start, handler prelude, real token probe/network overhead and platform scheduling delays.
No real database contention, CloudBase transaction retries, multi-instance race, large SKU batches or actual Apple/WeChat traffic is modeled.
Daily retention is modeled at repository-method granularity; production purgeExpiredData and purgeGrowthData contain multiple sequential operations that can overrun a nominal cleanup allowance.
HTTP and message cancellation are modeled from the budgets the code supplies, not by wall-clock platform transport execution.
A 15-second nominal reserve is not a hard bound on cleanup because existing database operations and settlement are not collectively deadline-cancelled.

The 45-second experiment measures throughput and bounded-network behavior; it does not change shared request quotas, concurrency, notification dedupe, uncertain-send retry semantics or platform remaining-time helper behavior.
